objective: Check whether SG057 fixed prefix-only early-abstain training policy transfers to five newly programmed disturbance mechanisms under the original frozen cost model.
method: SG057 fixed training from 810 SG052 traces at start 215000000. Authorized groups 220:unresolved:lt1:low and 220:unresolved:lt2:low. Evaluate 9 before/after sign pairings × five new mechanisms × 20 heldout seeds = 900 streams, with unknown programmed change onset 100/120/140. Comparator 240 final observation. Early policy observes 220 then abstains in authorized groups, otherwise 240.

pilot.disclosure: Pilot observed and logged before freeze; no retuning.

interpretation: Under fixed synthetic costs, early abstention decreases loss on all five newly defined disturbance families, including rare outlier, time-varying scale, level jump, burst oscillation and curvature. This is a synthetic constructed shift test, not proof of arbitrary disturbance or real-world robustness. 641 of 900 policy outcomes remain unresolved; nonlinear_bias 18 false-direction claims persists.
limitations: Generator types were constructed by the experimenter and still use SG052 sign-change schedule and truth labels.
The prefix-only audit used 900 equivalent full-record decisions and 270 suffix perturbation challenges; not a formal proof of arbitrary data-flow control.
Policy has high abstention (71.2%); user-facing deployment stakes unknown.
Modeled loss weights chosen before this holdout, not empirical cost estimates.
The GitHub-portable script was re-fetched but not independently run in clean checkout; the local equivalent was executed.
